title: Modernism, program and post-war public architecture
question: How did function, material and institutional program reshape architectural form within post-war modernism, and which links between housing, transport and cultural buildings are actually documented?
selection_rationale: The six-Feature set places collective housing, transport infrastructure and a national cultural institution beside two explicit precedents. The Olivier Theatre is represented separately from its parent complex so the Epidaurus transmission has an exact endpoint; Preston's broader Le Corbusier attribution remains deliberately unresolved at building level.

features.name: Unité d’Habitation, Marseille
features.selection_rationale: Provides the named housing precedent for Park Hill and an official account of the vertical-city program.

features.name: Park Hill, Sheffield
features.selection_rationale: Tests how a documented continental precedent was adapted to a municipal slum-clearance program, steep site and community-preservation objective.

features.name: Preston Central Bus Station and Car Park
features.selection_rationale: Adds integrated transport infrastructure whose official record names broad Le Corbusier influence but not a specific source building.

features.name: Royal National Theatre
features.selection_rationale: Provides the institutional and multi-auditorium parent complex without treating every part of it as derived from Epidaurus.

features.name: Olivier Theatre
features.selection_rationale: Provides the exact auditorium endpoint for the National Theatre archive's explicit Epidaurus influence statement.

features.name: Theatre of Epidaurus
features.selection_rationale: Supplies the explicit auditorium precedent named by the National Theatre archive and prevents the comparison from reducing program to material style.

claims.statement: The Marseille Unité contains 330 housing units.
claims.uncertainty: The official work record states the unit count but does not evaluate residents' later experience.

claims.statement: Its interior streets, shopping levels and roof facilities were organized as a vertical-city program rather than circulation alone.
claims.uncertainty: The source records the architect's programmatic conception; realized social outcomes require separate evidence.

claims.statement: Park Hill's wide access decks were designed as streets in the sky and as a means of recreating the community spirit of traditional streets.
claims.uncertainty: The designation record describes design intent and historical assessment, not a controlled measure of social success.

claims.statement: Historic England describes Park Hill as based on Le Corbusier's Unité d’Habitation in Marseille.
claims.uncertainty: The explicit statement appears in the contextual history of another Sheffield designation and does not itemize which Park Hill elements were adapted.

relation.qualifier: overall housing precedent; the source does not enumerate every borrowed element

claims.statement: Preston integrates a bus station, multi-storey car park and taxi rank in one civic complex.
claims.uncertainty: The heritage record establishes the integrated program but does not evaluate every user's experience of the complex.

claims.statement: Preston's official designation attributes its New Brutalist architecture to influence from late Le Corbusier but does not name a specific source building.
claims.uncertainty: The named influence is agent-level; narrowing it to Unité d’Habitation would exceed the locator.

claims.statement: The National Theatre organizes three auditoria within one public complex.
claims.uncertainty: The designation entry is concise and does not capture every later alteration or operational pattern.

claims.statement: The Theatre of Epidaurus was a major influence on Lasdun's design for the Olivier Theatre within the National Theatre.
claims.uncertainty: The relation applies specifically to the Olivier auditorium, not to every part of the National Theatre complex.

relation.qualifier: auditorium design, not the whole National Theatre complex

claims.statement: France's Minister of Reconstruction and Urbanism commissioned the Marseille Unité as a collective building within the post-war rehousing program.
claims.uncertainty: The source situates the commission within reconstruction policy but does not measure its comparative policy effectiveness.

claims.statement: Preston's precast-concrete decks use compound curves as a principal element of the building's architectural expression.
claims.uncertainty: The heritage assessment emphasizes design intent and surviving form rather than a complete engineering performance analysis.

conclusion.statement: Program is not a secondary label in this set: interior streets, integrated transport and auditorium organization shape the selected modern works. Two transmissions are documentable with exact endpoints—Park Hill from Unité and the Olivier Theatre from Epidaurus—while Preston's broader Le Corbusier attribution must remain agent-level and unresolved at the building level.

module_uncertainty: Park Hill's official record documents intent more strongly than resident outcomes.
The Park Hill–Unité relation needs a reviewer to test whether “based on” is best normalized as modelled_on or adapted_from.
Preston must not be linked to Unité solely because both evidence sets mention Le Corbusier.
The Epidaurus relation uses the Olivier Theatre as its exact endpoint rather than the whole National Theatre.
Claims and EvidenceLinks remain draft until both independent reviewers confirm the corrected frozen revision.
